subject: Moderation in lavaan with observed variables

messages.author: 960267f760064c0b
messages.subject: Moderation in lavaan with observed variables
parts:
Hi all,
I am trying to use lavaan to examine moderation between two observed variables instead of using other analytical strategies as I have been told that lavaan produce less bias in the estimation of standard errors. 
I want to examine whether the relationship between two observed variables is moderated by a multi-categorical variable (four categories). My questions are how to code in lavaan and how to know if there is moderation.
Thank you so much in advance,

Best regards,
Majeed

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Moderation in lavaan with observed variables
parts: I want to examine whether the relationship between two observed variables is moderated by a multi-categorical variable (four categories). My questions are how to code in lavaan and how to know if there is moderation.

You can use a single-group approach by creating dummy codes for 3 of the 4 categories and including their effects in the model syntax.  You can specify interaction terms to test moderation, using the colon operator.  

You can also use a multigroup approach, which I think is more intuitive, but in that case you should have a decent sample size (given the number of parameters you want to estimate) within each group.  Instead of using dummy codes, you would use the name of the grouping variable for the group= argument to the lavaan() function (or the sem() or cfa() wrappers).  You can test moderation by comparing models with and without constraining at least one regression slope to equality across groups.

There are some more details here:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/kkY-w10lOlE/4nEY-U1YBgAJ
